Hezbollah has significantly expanded its drone operations since March 2026, deploying fiber-optic-guided FPV drones that evade Israeli electronic countermeasures. BBC Verify geolocated 35 Hezbollah drone strike videos between late March and mid-May. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu described the fiber-optic drones as a major threat and ordered accelerated countermeasure development. The drone threat has prompted Israel to escalate air strikes across southern and eastern Lebanon.

title: Mandiant Discloses CVE-2026-5426 Zero-Day Exploited in KnowledgeDeliver LMS via ViewState Deserialization
summary: Google's Mandiant team disclosed CVE-2026-5426, a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Digital Knowledge's KnowledgeDeliver LMS, stemming from shared ASP.NET machine keys across deployments. Threat actors deployed BLUEBEAM web shells and Cobalt Strike payloads through crafted ViewState data.
contents:
## CVE-2026-5426 Vulnerability Disclosure

### Background
Mandiant responded to a security incident involving KnowledgeDeliver, a Learning Management System developed by Digital Knowledge and widely deployed in Japan. The investigation revealed a critical vulnerability that allowed unauthenticated Remote Code Execution through ViewState deserialization.

### Technical Details
KnowledgeDeliver installations deployed before February 24, 2026 relied on a standardized web.config file containing hardcoded ASP.NET machineKey values. Because these keys remained identical across independent customer environments, any threat actor who obtained the keys from one deployment could compromise any other internet-facing instance.

The vulnerability follows the same pattern observed in Sitecore ViewState deserialization attacks and publicly disclosed ASP.NET machine key exploitation campaigns documented by Microsoft.

### Post-Exploitation Activity
The threat actors deployed BLUEBEAM (Godzilla), a .NET-based in-memory web shell operating within the IIS worker process. They modified application JavaScript files to display fake security alerts, tricking users into installing a malicious plugin that loaded a remote script. This led to Cobalt Strike BEACON infections on user workstations, with payloads encrypted using keys tied to the targeted organization.

### Remediation
Organizations should immediately generate unique, cryptographically strong machine keys for each KnowledgeDeliver instance to invalidate the shared secret. Monitoring for Event ID 1316 from ASP.NET sources and suspicious w3wp.exe child processes provides detection opportunities.

### Impact Assessment
The exploitation of shared secrets in deployment templates represents a severe systemic risk, as a single leaked key can compromise an entire ecosystem of installations.

title: North Korea Launches Unidentified Projectile Toward Yellow Sea Amid Heightened Nuclear Concerns
summary: North Korea launched an unidentified projectile toward the Yellow Sea on May 26, 2026, as IAEA chief Grossi warned of 'very serious' progress in Pyongyang's nuclear weapons program and satellite imagery confirmed completion of a suspected uranium enrichment building at Yongbyon.
contents:
## North Korean Projectile Launch

### Launch Details
North Korea launched an unidentified projectile toward the Yellow Sea on May 26, 2026. South Korean and Japanese military authorities detected the launch and have begun analyzing the type and trajectory of the projectile. The launch comes amid intensified monitoring of North Korean nuclear facilities.

### Nuclear Program Developments
IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi recently stated that North Korea has made "very serious" progress in its nuclear weapons capabilities, with heightened activity observed at the Yongbyon Nuclear Research Center. A new building at Yongbyon, measuring approximately 120 by 48 meters with dimensions similar to the Kangson enrichment facility, now appears externally complete with internal fitting underway.

### Enrichment Expansion Concerns
The Beyond Parallel project at CSIS confirmed through satellite imagery from April 2026 that the suspected uranium enrichment building at Yongbyon has reached completion, featuring generators, fuel storage tanks, cooling units, and support buildings. The facility sits approximately 480 meters north-northeast of the Radiochemistry Laboratory.

### Estimated Arsenal
North Korea currently possesses an estimated 50 nuclear warheads according to security analysts, though experts continue debating whether Pyongyang has fully developed miniaturization technology for long-range ballistic missiles. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has warned that North Korea could produce enough fissile material annually to build between 10 and 20 additional nuclear weapons.

### Strategic Implications
The projectile launch and nuclear facility expansion occur against the backdrop of the ongoing Iran war, which has consumed significant U.S. military resources and attention, potentially providing North Korea additional space for provocative actions.

title: Russia Launches Large-Scale Overnight Drone and Missile Attack on Ukraine with Iskander-M and 122 UAVs
summary: Russia conducted a combined aerial attack on Ukraine overnight May 25-26 using two Iskander-M ballistic missiles and 122 strike UAVs including Shahed-type drones. Ukrainian air defenses neutralized 111 targets by 08:30 UTC, though nine strike UAVs and missiles hit targets across 11 locations.
contents:
## Overnight Aerial Assault on Ukraine

### Attack Composition
The Russian military launched a combined strike against Ukraine during the night of May 25-26, 2026, deploying two Iskander-M ballistic missiles alongside 122 strike UAVs. The unmanned aerial vehicles included Shahed-type attack drones as well as Gerbera, Italmas, and Parodiya decoy variants designed to overwhelm Ukrainian air defense systems.

### Air Defense Response
Ukraine's defense forces responded using aviation assets, anti-aircraft missile troops, electronic warfare units, unmanned systems, and mobile fire groups. By 08:30 UTC, preliminary data indicated that 111 UAVs fell to defensive fire or suppressed across northern, southern, and eastern regions of Ukraine.

### Strike Impact
Despite the high interception rate, nine strike UAVs and missiles successfully hit targets across 11 separate locations. Additionally, debris from intercepted drones fell in three locations, causing collateral damage. The Ukrainian Armed Forces warned that the aerial assault continued beyond the preliminary reporting period, with new groups of enemy UAVs entering Ukrainian airspace.

### Escalation Pattern
This attack represents part of a continuing pattern of large-scale Russian aerial bombardments. The Russian military has broken its own records for drone attacks three times during May 2026 alone, indicating a deliberate strategy of drone saturation to overwhelm Ukrainian defenses.

### Ongoing Threat
The Armed Forces of Ukraine issued a public warning: "The attack continues, new groups of enemy UAVs have entered Ukraine's airspace. Follow safety rules!" The continuous nature of these attacks strains Ukrainian air defense resources and ammunition supplies.

title: Ukraine Constructs Multi-Kilometer Anti-Tank Ditches and Bunkers Around Odessa
summary: Construction of multi-kilometer anti-tank ditches and bunkers around Odessa has begun, with barbed wire installed at city entry points, according to Ukraine's Southern Defense Forces. Officials stated the defensive structures serve to prevent a potential attack rather than respond to an imminent threat.
contents:
## Odessa Defensive Fortifications

### Construction Details
Ukraine's Southern Defense Forces have initiated construction of multi-kilometer anti-tank ditches and bunkers around the strategic port city of Odessa. Barbed wire installations now guard the entry points of the city, transforming the urban perimeter into a fortified defensive zone.

### Official Justification
Southern Defense Forces officials clarified that the defensive structures "prepare not because an attack on Odessa appears imminent but to prevent such an attack from happening." This preventive posture reflects growing concerns about potential Russian ground operations targeting Ukraine's key Black Sea port.

### Regional Context
The Odessa fortification effort follows similar defensive preparations in other Ukrainian regions. Authorities in the Kyiv and Volyn regions previously reported comparable defensive construction around populated areas, indicating a nationwide shift toward hardening urban defenses.

### Strategic Significance
Odessa represents Ukraine's primary remaining Black Sea port and a critical economic lifeline. The city's defense carries enormous strategic importance for Ukraine's ability to export grain and maintain international maritime trade connections. These fortifications aim to deter any Russian attempt to advance on the city through ground operations.

### Military Engineering Scope
The defensive works include anti-tank ditches designed to impede armored vehicle movement, reinforced bunker positions for infantry defense, and barbed wire barriers to channel and slow advancing forces. The multi-kilometer scale of the project suggests preparations for a comprehensive defensive perimeter around the city.

title: Israel Condemns Reburial of OUN Leader Andriy Melnyk in Ukraine
summary: Israel issued a condemnation of the reburial of Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN) leader Andriy Melnyk in Ukraine, highlighting tensions between historical memory and contemporary diplomatic relations between Israel and Ukraine.
contents:
## Israeli Condemnation of OUN Leader Reburial

### Diplomatic Response
Israel condemned the ceremonial reburial of Andriy Melnyk, a historical leader of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN), in Ukraine. The condemnation reflects deep sensitivities surrounding World War II-era Ukrainian nationalist movements and their controversial legacy.

### Historical Context
Andriy Melnyk led one faction of the OUN, a Ukrainian nationalist organization active during World War II. The OUN's historical record remains deeply contested, with some viewing members as freedom fighters against Soviet occupation while others point to documented collaboration with Nazi Germany and involvement in violence against Jewish and Polish populations.

### Diplomatic Implications
The Israeli condemnation introduces friction into Israel-Ukraine relations at a sensitive diplomatic juncture. Ukraine continues seeking international support amid its ongoing conflict with Russia, making any diplomatic complications with allied nations particularly unwelcome.

### Memory Politics
The reburial ceremony represents part of Ukraine's broader effort to honor historical figures associated with the independence movement. However, the commemoration of figures linked to wartime nationalist movements consistently generates international controversy, particularly from nations whose populations suffered during that period.

### Broader Pattern
This incident fits within an ongoing pattern of disputes between Israel and Eastern European nations over the commemoration of wartime figures with ambiguous or contested legacies.

title: Ukraine Mobilizes Influencers to Build European Support with Mixed Public Reception
summary: Ukraine launched an influencer campaign aimed at convincing European audiences that supporting Ukraine remains essential for their own security, though public comment sections showed significant pushback against the messaging strategy.
contents:
## Ukrainian Influencer Campaign for European Support

### Campaign Overview
Ukraine has deployed a coordinated influencer strategy targeting European audiences, seeking to frame continued support for Ukraine as directly relevant to European security interests. The campaign mobilizes Ukrainian content creators and social media personalities to deliver the message that failing to support Ukraine would leave European nations vulnerable to similar threats.

### Public Reception
The influencer initiative has met with notably mixed reception among European audiences. Comment sections beneath the campaign content showed significant disagreement with the messaging, suggesting that public fatigue with the conflict narrative and skepticism toward orchestrated influence campaigns may limit effectiveness.

### Strategic Communications Context
The campaign reflects Ukraine's recognition that maintaining European public support requires active engagement beyond traditional diplomatic channels. As the conflict extends into its fourth year, sustaining public attention and financial commitment from European partners has become increasingly challenging.

### Information Environment
The initiative operates within a contested information environment where Russian counter-narratives compete for European public opinion. The visible pushback in comment sections demonstrates the complexity of conducting influence operations in democratized media spaces where audiences can immediately challenge official narratives.

### Implications for Alliance Cohesion
The mixed response highlights a growing gap between governmental support for Ukraine across the European Union and public sentiment, which war fatigue and economic pressures from the ongoing Iran conflict and energy price disruptions continue to erode.

title: Russian Strikes on Odesa Kill One and Injure Three Amid Ongoing Aerial Campaign
summary: Russian military strikes on Odesa killed one person and injured three others on May 26, 2026, as Moscow continued its intensifying aerial bombardment campaign across Ukraine while peace negotiations with the United States remained stalled over enriched uranium disposition.
contents:
## Russian Strikes on Odesa

### Attack Details
Russian military forces struck the port city of Odesa on May 26, 2026, killing one person and injuring three others. The attack formed part of Moscow's sustained aerial campaign targeting Ukrainian urban centers and infrastructure.

### Escalation Pattern
The Odesa strikes occurred alongside a large-scale overnight drone and missile attack involving two Iskander-M ballistic missiles and 122 strike UAVs launched against multiple Ukrainian regions. The pattern of intensifying Russian aerial attacks has seen Moscow break its own records for drone bombardments three times during May 2026.

### Strategic Context
Odesa holds critical strategic importance as Ukraine's primary remaining Black Sea port. Ukrainian authorities have recently begun constructing multi-kilometer anti-tank ditches and bunker positions around the city, reflecting heightened concerns about potential Russian ground operations targeting the port.

### Diplomatic Backdrop
The attack came as U.S. Secretary of State Rubio indicated that Iran deal talks remained ongoing, with final text potentially requiring additional days. The simultaneous U.S. focus on the Iran war has drawn criticism from Ukrainian officials who argue that American attention and military resources shifted away from supporting Ukraine's defense.

### Impact on Civilian Life
Russian strikes on Odesa repeatedly targeted civilian areas and port infrastructure, disrupting grain exports and damaging the city's cultural heritage sites. The continued attacks undermine humanitarian conditions for the city's remaining population.

title: Taiwan Defense Minister Calls for Additional Missile and Artillery Systems to Counter Growing PLA Capabilities
summary: Taiwan's Defense Minister Wellington Koo urged procurement of M109A7 howitzers, HIMARS, and anti-armor drone missile systems, citing improvements in China's strike, amphibious assault, and joint operations capabilities as the legislature approved a special defense budget.
contents:
## Taiwan Missile Procurement Push

### Defense Minister's Assessment
Taiwan's Minister of National Defense Wellington Koo addressed the legislature's Foreign Affairs and National Defense Committee on May 25-26, stating that Taiwan must procure additional missile and artillery systems to counter improvements China has made to its strike, amphibious assault, and joint operations capabilities.

### Procurement List
Koo outlined plans to purchase M109A7 self-propelled howitzers with GPS-guided automated fire control, High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems (HIMARS) capable of conducting deep strikes within a 300-kilometer range, anti-armor drone missile systems, and TOW 2B anti-armor missiles.

### Legislative Budget Approval
The legislature on May 8 passed a special defense budget authorizing up to NT$300 billion (approximately US$9.53 billion) for a first round of U.S. arms purchases and NT$480 billion for a second round. The first procurement package totals NT$294.99 billion.

### Russia-Ukraine War Lessons
Drawing lessons from the Russia-Ukraine conflict, Koo emphasized that precision ground firepower could target enemy command posts, logistics hubs, and communications centers. He described how the PLA's strategy has shifted from traditional beachhead assaults to rapid multidomain operations aimed at establishing air superiority before launching amphibious invasion operations.

### Three-Phase Defense Framework
Koo outlined how the new systems would support Taiwan across three phases: integrated air and missile defense, anti-landing operations, and homeland defense. He emphasized the growing importance of drones, AI-assisted decision-making systems, and integrated battlefield communications networks in bolstering asymmetric warfare capabilities.

title: NATO Narrow Waters 26-1 Naval Exercises Underway in Gulf of Finland with US, German, and Finnish Forces
summary: NATO launched the Narrow Waters 26-1 naval exercises in the Gulf of Finland from May 20-27, involving approximately 3,000 military personnel from the United States, Germany, and Finland, focusing on joint operations, coastal defense, and widespread use of marine unmanned systems.
contents:
## NATO Narrow Waters 26-1 Exercises

### Exercise Overview
The Narrow Waters 26-1 naval maneuvers commenced in the Gulf of Finland on May 20, running through May 27, 2026. The exercise involves approximately 3,000 military personnel from the United States, Germany, and Finland, focusing on joint operations in the northern Baltic, coastal defense, archipelago operations, and the widespread use of marine unmanned systems.

### Regional Security Context
The exercise occurs alongside a series of NATO activities reinforcing the Alliance's posture along its eastern flank. Earlier in May, the Amber Shock 26 exercises positioned American troops in northeastern Poland near the Kaliningrad region, while the Northern Strike 26 maneuvers brought nine NATO nations together near the Finnish-Russian border.

### Royal Navy Leadership
NATO's Standing NATO Maritime Group 1 (SNMG1) recently transitioned to Royal Navy command under Commodore Maryla Ingham, operating from the German flagship FGS Sachsen. SNMG1 continues patrolling critical waterways and chokepoints across the North Atlantic, Arctic, and Baltic regions.

### Unmanned Systems Focus
The exercise places particular emphasis on marine unmanned systems, reflecting NATO's growing investment in autonomous underwater vehicles and unmanned surface vessels for mine countermeasures, surveillance, and anti-submarine warfare missions.

### Baltic Security Architecture
These exercises complement the recently concluded Open Spirit 26 mine countermeasures drill and ongoing Baltic Sentry operations protecting critical underwater infrastructure, including pipelines and communications cables, from potential sabotage or surveillance.

title: CENTCOM Reports Defensive Strikes Against Iranian Missile Sites and Naval Vessels in Strait of Hormuz Operations
summary: U.S. Central Command reported conducting defensive strikes against Iranian missile sites and naval vessels as part of ongoing Strait of Hormuz operations, where commercial shipping traffic has dropped to approximately 5 percent of pre-conflict levels.
contents:
## CENTCOM Defensive Maritime Operations

### Operational Report
The United States Central Command disclosed that U.S. forces conducted defensive strikes against Iranian missile sites and boats as part of continuing operations to secure the Strait of Hormuz and protect coalition forces in the region. The strikes targeted assets posing direct threats to naval operations.

### Maritime Security Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to Western-allied commercial traffic, with shipping volumes plunging to approximately 5 percent of pre-conflict levels. Lloyd's List Intelligence assessed the strait as closed with no Western-allied transits recorded since early May 2026. The International Maritime Organization has declared both U.S. and Iranian ship seizures violations of international maritime law.

### IRGC Toll Regime
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has established a "Persian Gulf Strait Authority" toll regime, charging per-vessel transit fees of up to $2 million payable in Chinese yuan, Bitcoin, or USDT. The oil tanker fee structure reportedly sits at approximately $0.50 to $1 per barrel of crude cargo.

### Global Economic Impact
The Hormuz closure threatens approximately $1.2 trillion in annual global trade. Brent crude prices remain elevated above $103 per barrel, having surged more than 60 percent since the conflict began on February 27, 2026. The IEA Director General characterized the closure as "the biggest energy security threat in history."

### Naval Force Posture
Three U.S. carrier strike groups currently operate in the theater: USS Abraham Lincoln, USS Gerald R. Ford, and USS George H.W. Bush, supported by multiple guided-missile destroyers and over 100 aircraft.

title: Taiwan Tracks Second Chinese Joint Combat Readiness Patrol in One Week, Deploys Ships and Jets
summary: Taiwan detected 21 Chinese aircraft including J-16 fighters and drones conducting a joint combat readiness patrol around the island, the second such patrol in one week, as tensions remain elevated following Xi Jinping's Taiwan discussions with Trump.
contents:
## Chinese Combat Patrol Around Taiwan

### Patrol Detection
Taiwan's defense ministry detected 21 Chinese aircraft, including J-16 fighters and unmanned aerial vehicles, operating around the island on May 25-26, accompanied by warships conducting what Beijing designates a "joint combat readiness patrol." Taiwan deployed its own ships and fighter jets to monitor the Chinese military activities.

### Second Patrol in One Week
This patrol marks the second Chinese combat readiness operation around Taiwan within seven days. The previous patrol occurred one day before Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te marked his second year in office. China characterizes Lai as a "separatist" and has rebuffed multiple offers from him for dialogue.

### Surveillance Evidence
Taiwan's defense ministry published photographs taken by its forces, including an image from an F-16 jet showing two Chinese fighters trailing a Y-20 aerial refueling aircraft, the Chinese warship Yinchuan, and a Taiwanese navy sailor observing the vessel through binoculars.

### Carrier Group Tracking
Taiwan continues monitoring the movements of China's aircraft carrier Liaoning operating in the Western Pacific. Taiwan's National Security Council Secretary-General Joseph Wu detailed approximately 100 Chinese ships currently deployed across the first island chain, stretching from Japan through Taiwan into the Philippines.

### Pratas Islands Standoff
The combat patrol follows a separate maritime confrontation near the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands, where a Chinese coast guard vessel engaged in a 20-hour standoff with Taiwanese ships before departing. Taiwan's coast guard has expelled Chinese vessels from Pratas restricted waters in six incidents since the start of 2026.

contents:
## Ukrainian Strikes on Enemy Command Infrastructure and Logistics

### Targeted Operations on May 25-26, 2026

Ukrainian defense forces conducted a series of precision strikes against critical enemy military infrastructure on May 25 and overnight into May 26, 2026.

### Command and Control Strikes

Forces struck an enemy command post in Ocheretyne, Donetsk Oblast, and a regimental control point in Verkhnya Krynytsia, Zaporizhzhia Oblast. UAV control points belonging to the occupying forces near Nesterianka in Zaporizhzhia and Novohrodivka in Donetsk Oblast also sustained damage.

Additionally, the destruction of an enemy 1L125 Niobium-SV radar station near Yarsk, Luhansk Oblast, targeted on May 24, received confirmation.

Ukrainian defense forces have committed to continuing systematic measures to compel Russia to cease its armed aggression against Ukraine.

## Paratrooper Oath Ceremony at 199th Training Center

### Event Overview

The 199th Training Center of the Airborne Assault Forces in Zhytomyr hosted one of the most demanding and honorable stages of warrior formation — the Paratrooper Oath ritual for first-year cadets of the Airborne Assault Forces and Marine Infantry faculty at the Odesa Military Academy.

### Rigorous Testing Program

Ten teams of cadets underwent a grueling trial of strength, endurance, character, and brotherhood. On their path to earning the coveted maroon beret, the paratroopers overcame more than 10 complex stages designed to push them beyond their limits.

### Stages of the Ceremony

The cadets navigated a psychological obstacle course through smoke-filled terrain and mud. They endured tank run-overs, engaged in combat action drills, carried heavy loads, evacuated military vehicles, crossed water obstacles via suspended rope bridges, and completed combat sparring sessions.

### Military Training Significance

This ceremony represents a critical milestone in the professional development of Ukrainian airborne troops, forging the next generation of elite soldiers who will defend their nation. The 199th Training Center continues to maintain rigorous standards for Airborne Assault Forces personnel preparation.

The Communications Group of the 199th Training Center of the Airborne Assault Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine provided this report.

title: Survey Reveals Russian Public Trust in Putin Falls to Critical 10.5 Percent
summary: A USP survey shows that belief Russia follows the right course has plummeted to 10.5%. A record 84% of respondents blame Putin for the 2026 large-scale fires, and 73.8% consider living in Russia dangerous. Telegram blocking and internet restrictions further eroded public confidence.
contents:
## Russian Public Confidence in Putin Reaches Historic Low

### Survey Findings

Recent USP survey data reveals that Russian public trust in President Putin has fallen to critical levels. The proportion of respondents who believe Russia follows the "right course" has dropped to just 10.5%, representing a dramatic erosion of confidence in the country’s leadership.

### Blame for National Crises

A record 84% of survey respondents hold Putin responsible for the large-scale fires across Russia in 2026, including the devastating fires in Tuapse. This finding suggests that Russians increasingly connect national disasters directly to presidential leadership failures rather than viewing them as isolated incidents.

### Personal Safety Concerns

The survey found that 73.8% of Russians now consider living in Russia dangerous — a remarkable shift in public sentiment that reflects growing anxiety about domestic security, infrastructure failures, and the ongoing consequences of military operations abroad.

### Digital Restrictions Fuel Discontent

Another major source of public frustration emerged from the government’s blocking of Telegram and broader internet restrictions. These digital crackdowns undermined trust in Putin to a degree comparable to the oil refinery fires, indicating that information access has become a core governance issue for Russian citizens.

### Broader Implications

The convergence of multiple crises — military setbacks, infrastructure disasters, economic pressures, and digital repression — appears to have created a compounding effect on Russian public opinion. The survey data points to a population increasingly disillusioned with the current trajectory of Russian governance and leadership.

title: JNIM Releases Footage of April 25 Coordinated Attacks on Military Targets Across Mali
summary: Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) prepared to release video footage documenting coordinated attacks carried out on April 25 against military positions in Kati-Bamako, Sévaré, Kidal, and Gao. The footage reveals the use of rudimentary armaments including 14.5mm and 12.7mm weapons alongside tactical drone deployment.
contents:
## JNIM Multi-City Attack Documentation Released

### Overview
Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM), the al-Qaeda-affiliated jihadist coalition operating across the Sahel, prepared to disseminate combat footage from its April 25, 2026 coordinated assault on four major Malian military installations. The attacks struck simultaneously at Kati (near Bamako, the capital), Sévaré, Kidal, and Gao, representing one of the largest multi-city operations by the group in recent months.

### Tactical Assessment
Analysis of the forthcoming footage by Wassim Nasr, a leading expert on Sahel jihadism at France 24, highlighted the notable use of rudimentary heavy weaponry — specifically 14.5mm and 12.7mm caliber weapons — alongside tactical drone deployment. This combination of low-tech firepower with emerging drone capabilities reflects JNIM's evolving military doctrine, which blends conventional insurgent tactics with newer technologies adapted from conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East.

### Strategic Context
The coordinated strikes targeted the Malian military junta, demonstrating JNIM's sustained operational reach across Mali's vast territory. The selection of Kati, home to Mali's primary military base just outside Bamako, underscores the group's willingness to project force near the seat of government power. The simultaneous targeting of Sévaré, Kidal, and Gao — key garrison towns — suggests sophisticated planning and inter-cell coordination.

### Regional Implications
The release of this footage serves both operational and propaganda purposes for JNIM. By documenting successful strikes against multiple hardened military targets, the group aims to demonstrate continued capability despite ongoing French departure from the region and the arrival of Russian Wagner Group forces. The tactical drone usage marks a significant evolution in Sahelian insurgent warfare methodology.

title: Arrest of Salafist Preacher Mohamad Kindo Signals Rupture in Burkina Faso Junta-Islamist Alliance
summary: The arrest of prominent Salafist preacher Mohamad Kindo in Burkina Faso appeared to end the tactical alliance between Salafist movements and Captain Ibrahim Traoré's military junta. The development mirrors historical patterns of authoritarian-Salafist cooperation observed in Libya with Haftar and in Egypt with Sissi.
contents:
## Burkina Faso Junta-Salafist Alliance Fractures

### Overview
Burkina Faso authorities detained Salafist preacher Mohamad Kindo, signaling a significant rupture in the tacit alliance between the ruling military junta and Salafist religious movements. The arrest drew immediate analytical attention from Sahel security experts who noted the historical precedent of such partnerships between authoritarian military leaders and ultraconservative religious figures.

### Historical Pattern
According to Wassim Nasr, a France 24 journalist specializing in jihadism and Sahel security, the Kindo-Traoré alliance followed a well-documented pattern of Salafist movements supporting military strongmen across the Muslim world. Comparable alliances have included Salafist groups backing Khalifa Haftar in Libya during the civil war and ultraconservative religious movements supporting Abdel Fattah el-Sissi's seizure of power in Egypt. These partnerships typically serve mutual short-term interests: military leaders gain religious legitimacy, while Salafist movements obtain space to operate and expand their influence.

### Implications for Regional Security
The arrest suggests Captain Traoré's government now views the Salafist movement as a liability rather than an asset. This shift could push marginalized Salafist networks toward radicalization or toward alignment with existing jihadist groups operating in the Sahel region, potentially complicating the already fragile security landscape across West Africa's conflict-affected zones.

### Broader Context
Burkina Faso remains one of the most violence-affected countries in the Sahel, with JNIM and Islamic State affiliate ISGS conducting regular attacks against military and civilian targets. The junta's decision to arrest a prominent religious figure risks opening a new domestic front while simultaneously fighting an active insurgency.

title: One-Year Anniversary of Israeli Strike on Fahmi Al-Jarjawi School in Gaza City Marks Ongoing Civilian Toll
summary: The one-year mark passed since Israeli forces struck the Fahmi Al-Jarjawi School in Gaza City, where displaced families had taken shelter. The attack killed at least 36 civilians, including children and women, transforming the school into a scene of destruction.
contents:
## Gaza School Attack Anniversary

### Overview
One year elapsed since Israeli military forces carried out a devastating strike on the Fahmi Al-Jarjawi School in Gaza City on May 26, 2025. The school had functioned as a shelter for displaced Palestinian families seeking refuge from ongoing military operations in the Gaza Strip. The attack killed at least 36 civilians, including numerous children and women.

### Context of the Attack
The targeting of educational facilities repurposed as displacement shelters became a recurring pattern throughout the Gaza conflict. International humanitarian organizations repeatedly condemned strikes on schools, hospitals, and other civilian infrastructure designated as shelters for internally displaced persons. The Fahmi Al-Jarjawi School represented one of dozens of UNRWA and government-operated facilities that sustained direct hits during military operations.

### Humanitarian Impact
The strike reduced the school to rubble, killing entire families sheltering within its walls. Survivors described scenes of chaos and devastation, with rescue workers struggling to extract victims from collapsed structures. The attack drew widespread international condemnation and contributed to mounting calls for accountability regarding civilian casualties in the conflict.

### Continuing Crisis
The anniversary arrives amid continued hostilities in the Gaza Strip, where Palestinian civilians remain trapped in a humanitarian catastrophe marked by widespread displacement, infrastructure destruction, and limited access to medical care, food, and clean water. Human rights organizations continue documenting civilian casualties and calling for adherence to international humanitarian law by all parties.

title: Pro-Palestine Climbers Raise Gaza Children's Messages to Mount Everest Summit
summary: Pro-Palestine climbers carried a kite with messages from children in the Gaza Strip to the summit of Mount Everest, aiming to draw global attention to the suffering of Palestinian children under ongoing Israeli bombardment and blockade.
contents:
## Everest Summit Solidarity Action for Gaza

### Overview
Pro-Palestine mountaineers successfully carried a kite inscribed with messages from children living in the Gaza Strip to the summit of Mount Everest, the world's highest peak at 8,849 meters. The symbolic action aimed to amplify the voices of Palestinian children experiencing the effects of relentless Israeli military operations and the ongoing blockade of the territory.

### Symbolic Significance
The choice of Mount Everest — the highest point on Earth — served as a deliberate metaphor for elevating Palestinian children's stories to the widest possible global audience. The kite, a traditional symbol of childhood freedom and play, carried handwritten messages from young Gazans describing their experiences of displacement, loss, and hope. The action connected the imagery of children's aspirations with the extreme physical achievement of summiting Everest.

### International Solidarity Movement
The climb represented part of a broader pattern of creative international solidarity actions undertaken by activists seeking to maintain global attention on the humanitarian situation in Gaza. Previous actions have included marathon runs, art installations, flotillas, and diplomatic campaigns. The Everest action attracted significant attention on social media, generating widespread engagement across platforms.

### Context
The solidarity action coincided with continued military operations in the Gaza Strip, where civilian infrastructure remains extensively damaged and humanitarian access restricted. International organizations have documented severe impacts on children's physical and psychological well-matched throughout the conflict period, with displacement affecting over a million young Palestinians.

title: US Forces Conduct Self-Defense Strikes on Southern Iran Targeting Missile Sites and Mine-Laying Boats
summary: US Central Command carried out strikes near Bandar Abbas in southern Iran, targeting missile launch sites and Iranian boats attempting to lay mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The strikes occurred amid ongoing ceasefire and active negotiations in Doha for a potential deal to end the conflict.
contents:
## US Military Strikes Southern Iran Near Strait of Hormuz

### Overview
US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced self-defense strikes against targets in southern Iran on May 26, 2026. The military action targeted missile launch sites and Iranian boats attempting to emplace mines near the Strait of Hormuz, according to CENTCOM spokesperson Navy Captain Tim Hawkins.

### Details of the Operation
The strikes hit targets near Bandar Abbas, a major port city and Iranian naval base located approximately 70 kilometers from the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian media reported explosions in Bandar Abbas city and surrounding coastal areas. Two Iranian boats engaged in mine-laying operations faced destruction by US forces, according to a senior US official cited by Fox News. A surface-to-air missile site in Bandar Abbas also sustained strikes after targeting US warplanes.

### Diplomatic Context
The military action came as an Iranian delegation, including Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, traveled to Doha, Qatar for negotiations. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated the Strait of Hormuz "has to open one way or the other" and estimated a deal could take "a few days." President Trump characterized negotiations as "proceeding nicely" but warned of escalation if talks failed. Iran's Foreign Ministry confirmed progress on a "large portion" of issues under discussion while denying an agreement remained imminent.

### Strategic Significance
The Strait of Hormuz carries approximately one-fifth of global oil and gas flows under normal conditions. The waterway has remained under de facto Iranian blockade since the conflict began on February 28. A proposed memorandum of understanding reportedly covers a 60-day ceasefire extension, reopening of the strait, and a framework for nuclear negotiations.

title: North Korea Launches Multiple Short-Range Ballistic Missiles Toward West Sea
summary: North Korea fired several short-range ballistic missiles from Jongju city toward the West Sea on May 26, marking the first weapons launch since April 19 and the eighth such test in 2026. South Korea, the US, and Japan heightened surveillance in response.
contents:
## North Korea Conducts Ballistic Missile Test

### Launch Details
North Korea launched multiple short-range ballistic missiles and other projectiles at approximately 1:00 PM local time on May 26, 2026, from the vicinity of Jongju (Chongju) city in North Pyongan Province. The missiles flew approximately 80 kilometers toward the West Sea (Yellow Sea), the body of water separating the Korean Peninsula from China.

### Military Response
South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff detected the launches and bolstered surveillance posture immediately. Military authorities confirmed close information-sharing with the United States and Japan regarding North Korean ballistic missile activity. The trilateral coordination reflects established protocols for monitoring Pyongyang's weapons programs.

### Context and Significance
The launch marks North Korea's first weapons test since April 19, when the country fired several short-range missiles described by state media as equipped with cluster bomb warheads. Analysts interpret the continued testing as part of North Korea's effort to demonstrate capacity for modern warfare, including cluster munitions and electromagnetic weapons.

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un declared in March that his country's nuclear-armed status remains irreversible and that expanding the "self-defensive nuclear deterrent" constitutes a national security essential. Pyongyang has ignored repeated overtures from the Trump administration to resume denuclearization talks.

### South Korean Response
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, during a Cabinet meeting the same day, called for accelerated efforts to acquire nuclear-powered submarines and urged prompt transfer of wartime operational control from Washington to Seoul. Lee emphasized the importance of demonstrating "the resolve to take responsibility for and protect our own security ourselves."

title: NASA Awards Lunar Terrain Vehicle Contracts to Astrolab and Lunar Outpost for Moon Base Program

contents:
## NASA Moon Base Rover Partnerships Announced

### Contract Awards
NASA announced new partnerships with Astrolab and Lunar Outpost for the development of lunar terrain vehicles during a Moon Base event at NASA Headquarters in Washington on May 26, 2026. The selected providers will finalize rover designs over the next 18 months for vehicles astronauts will operate on the lunar surface.

### Vehicle Capabilities
The Crewed Lunar Vehicle program encompasses rovers designed to transport astronauts across the lunar surface, carry supplies between locations, and support remote operations. Astrolab received a lunar terrain vehicle award for their Crewed Lunar Vehicle, a rover specifically engineered for astronaut transport and supply movement across lunar terrain. The vehicle targets deployment to the Moon by 2028 through NASA's commercial lunar payload services.

### Program Scope
The announcement formed part of a broader Moon Base update covering upcoming missions, new lander contracts, and the overall program for establishing long-term presence on the Moon. NASA partnered with commercial companies including Blue Origin and Astrobotic alongside the rover providers. The agency's approach leverages commercial partnerships to accelerate lunar infrastructure development while maintaining government oversight of mission objectives.

### Significance for Lunar Exploration
The rover contracts represent a critical step toward sustained human activity on the Moon. Previous Apollo-era rovers operated for limited durations during single missions. The new vehicles aim to support extended operations across multiple missions, enabling astronauts to explore greater distances from landing sites and maintain continuous supply chains between lunar facilities.

title: Remnants of Assad's Chemical Weapons Program Recovered by Syrian Officials
summary: Syrian officials announced the recovery of remnants from the Assad regime's chemical weapons program. The discovery came amid ongoing efforts to account for Syria's declared and undeclared chemical weapons capabilities following the regime's fall.
contents:
## Syrian Chemical Weapons Program Remnants Discovered

### Discovery
Syrian officials announced on May 26, 2026, that remnants of the Assad regime's chemical weapons program have undergone recovery. The announcement, reported by Reuters, marks a significant development in the long-running effort to account for Syria's chemical weapons stockpile.

### Historical Context
The Assad regime's chemical weapons program drew international condemnation following multiple attacks on civilian populations during the Syrian civil war. The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) oversaw the declared destruction of Syria's chemical weapons stockpile beginning in 2013, but questions persisted about undeclared facilities and hidden materials. International investigators documented continued chemical attacks even after the declared destruction, suggesting the regime retained undisclosed capabilities.

### Intelligence Implications
The recovery of program remnants provides new evidence about the scope and nature of the Assad regime's chemical weapons infrastructure. Intelligence community analysts have long assessed that Syria maintained undeclared chemical weapons research and production capabilities beyond what the regime disclosed to international inspectors. The new findings may offer valuable intelligence about production methods, precursor chemicals, and delivery mechanisms employed by the former regime.

### Ongoing Accountability
The discovery connects to broader international efforts to ensure accountability for chemical weapons use and prevent proliferation. The OPCW continues to investigate historical chemical attacks attributed to the Syrian regime, and recovered materials may contribute to ongoing forensic and intelligence assessments.

title: UK Sanctions Huobi Global and Crypto Exchanges in Major Russia Sanctions-Evasion Crackdown
summary: The UK government designated Huobi Global S.A. (HTX), EXMO Exchange, and Bitpapa alongside 18 other entities under Russia sanctions for facilitating sanctioned financial flows. The action marks the first application of Regulation 17A to cryptocurrency exchanges.
contents:
## UK Designates Major Crypto Exchanges Under Russia Sanctions

### Designation Details
The UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office announced on May 26, 2026, a sweeping sanctions package targeting Russian sanctions-evasion networks. The package includes 18 new designations under the Russia (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, with three cryptocurrency exchanges — Huobi Global S.A. (operator of HTX), EXMO Exchange Limited, and Bitpapa IC FZC LLC — among the designated entities.

### Regulatory Significance
The designation of HTX represents the first time the UK government has applied Regulation 17A to a cryptoasset exchange, establishing a precedent for sanctions enforcement against digital asset platforms. HTX reported $3.3 trillion in trading volume for 2025, making it one of the largest crypto exchanges ever directly sanctioned by a Western government. The exchange, originally founded in China as Huobi and rebranded under the advisory influence of crypto entrepreneur Justin Sun, operates with registration in Panama.

### Alleged Violations
The UK government cited HTX's alleged provision of financial services to A7 Limited Liability Company, a sanctioned Russian payments network. Authorities also highlighted connections between HTX and Garantex Europe OU, an entity previously targeted by regulators for facilitating illicit Russian financial flows through cryptocurrency channels.

### Broader Package
Beyond crypto exchanges, the sanctions package targets entities involved in supporting the Russian financial sector and making funds available to sanctioned Russian actors. Designated entities include Open Joint Stock Company 'Eurasian Savings Bank,' Diamond Estate LLC, and several individuals linked to sanctions circumvention networks. The UK simultaneously designated entities involved in virtual asset issuance and state brokerage operations connected to the Russian government.

### Implications
Any UK-based individuals or entities holding assets on HTX or conducting business with Huobi Global S.A. now face asset freeze restrictions. The action signals an expansion of Western sanctions enforcement into the cryptocurrency sector as regulators target digital asset platforms used to circumvent financial restrictions on Russia.

title: Iran Expands PGSA Maritime Authority Zone to UAE Coast as Trump Announces Deal Largely Negotiated
summary: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority extended its claimed zone to the UAE coast near Fujairah, drawing rejection from five Gulf states. Simultaneously, Trump announced a deal has emerged as largely negotiated, with Rubio confirming the Strait must open one way or another.
contents:
## Iran Expands Hormuz Authority Zone Amid Deal Negotiations

### PGSA Zone Expansion
Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) published an extended zone boundary on May 20 that reaches from the Strait of Hormuz across the Gulf of Oman to the UAE coast south of Fujairah. The extension encompasses the maritime approaches to the UAE's primary Hormuz-bypass oil export terminal, representing a significant escalation of Iran's claimed maritime authority.

### Gulf State Response
Five Gulf states — the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Qatar — formally rejected the expanded zone in a joint letter to the International Maritime Organization (IMO). The coalition warned commercial vessels not to engage with the PGSA or transit the Iran-designated route. The UKMTO simultaneously published its first dedicated Strait of Hormuz transit guidance for commercial shipping.

### Observable Impact
Within 24 hours of the announcement, chemical tanker AIS suppression spiked 59% in the Fujairah area. Crude exports from Fujairah fell to a six-month low, and VLCC counts dropped from 23 to 14. Fujairah's total wet cargo exports for the week hit 4.69 million barrels — the lowest in six months against an average of approximately 13 million barrels.

### US Enforcement Continues
US Marines boarded the Iranian-flagged tanker CELESTIAL SEA in the Gulf of Oman on May 20, the fourth at-sea interdiction of the enforcement campaign. CENTCOM has redirected 97 commercial ships and disabled 4 since the blockade began on April 13. Approximately 39.79 million barrels of Iran-origin oil now sit in floating storage across 79 tankers.

### Diplomatic Framework
President Trump publicly stated on May 23 that an agreement has emerged as "largely negotiated" — the first announced diplomatic resolution framework of the conflict. A proposed memorandum of understanding reportedly encompasses a 60-day ceasefire extension and the reopening of the Strait.

title: NATO Military Chiefs Demand Dramatic Defense Production Increase Ahead of Ankara Summit
summary: NATO's top military commanders called for a dramatic increase in European defense production following a meeting of the alliance's 32 chiefs of defense. Admiral Cavo Dragone firmly called on defense industry to accelerate production and end fragmentation.
contents:
## NATO Military Command Demands Defense Production Overhaul

### Chiefs of Defense Meeting
NATO's 32 chiefs of defense met in Brussels in the week of May 19, 2026, with the alliance's top military commanders issuing an urgent call for dramatically increased European defense production. The meeting preceded the upcoming NATO Ankara Summit, where allies will review billions in spending commitments.

### Key Statements
Admiral Pierre Vandier, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Transformation, declared that "NATO 3.0 doesn't exist without a defence industry 3.0" and demanded "more missiles, more ships, more air defence, more high-end capabilities, more stockpiles." Admiral Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, chair of the NATO Military Committee, delivered a blunt assessment: "We must note that the rate of delivery and refuelling of all capabilities necessary for our deterrence and defence requires a dramatic increase and improvement."

Cavo Dragone directed his criticism at the defense industry directly, calling firmly on manufacturers to "accelerate production and adapt their business models to this imperative. Enough with fragmentation." Military staffs hold "extremely high" expectations ahead of the Ankara Summit.

### Strategic Context
The urgency reflects Europe's continued reliance on the US for key capabilities despite pledges to increase production since Russia's invasion of Ukraine. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte has spearheaded a campaign to bring evidence of increased production and industrial contracts to the July summit, encouraging joint ventures with American defense firms and more US arms sales. About 51% of European NATO equipment spending between 2022 and 2024 went to the US, up from 28% in 2019-2021.

### US Troop Redeployment
General Alexus Grynkewich, Supreme Allied Commander Europe, addressed the recent US announcement to withdraw 5,000 troops from Europe, promising "no impact on the implementation of NATO's regional plans" while acknowledging that further redeployments should follow as European allies strengthen capabilities.
